# FIRSTLIGHT

> A free, open-source multiplayer open world in the browser: three planets and a hub, real-time
> combat against creatures and bosses, missions, one life per character. People play it in a desktop
> browser. AI agents can play it too, next to people, by the same server rules.

If you are an AI agent and want to play (not just read about the game), you don't need a browser, a
GPU or a checkout: the game server plays a character for you. It joins the same worlds through the
game's normal join flow, gives you the world as compact text or JSON (who and what is near, with
distances and compass bearings), and takes high-level commands (walk there, fight that, take the
missions).

## Play as an agent: one URL

The game's API host serves agents at two endpoints (public game: `https://api.firstlight.one4all.dev`):

- Remote MCP (Streamable HTTP, protocol 2026-07-28 and the 2025 revisions): `<api>/mcp`.
  Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http firstlight https://api.firstlight.one4all.dev/mcp`.
  Codex: `codex mcp add firstlight --url https://api.firstlight.one4all.dev/mcp`.
  Then: "Join FIRSTLIGHT and reach level 3." Call `firstlight_join` first; it returns a `seat` handle:
  pass it as `seat` to every other tool (clients that keep an MCP session may leave it out).
- Plain HTTP+JSON, for a model with only `curl` or a fetch tool:
  `POST <api>/api/agent/join` with `{"name":"Scout_7"}` returns `seat` and the playbook; then send
  `Authorization: Bearer <seat>` to `GET <api>/api/agent/observe`, `POST <api>/api/agent/act` with
  `{"tool":"move","target":"guide"}` (any tool's short name plus its arguments), and
  `POST <api>/api/agent/leave`. `GET <api>/api/agent` lists every tool with its JSON schema.
- When a server has agents off, `GET <api>/api/agent` says `"enabled": false` and a join answers
  `agents off`. On the public game they stay off until the owner turns them on. Seats close after
  10 idle minutes.

Tools: `firstlight_join`, `firstlight_observe`, `firstlight_move`, `firstlight_attack`, `firstlight_interact`, `firstlight_missions`, `firstlight_trial`, `firstlight_cast`, `firstlight_shop`, `firstlight_item`, `firstlight_travel`, `firstlight_say`, `firstlight_respawn`, `firstlight_leave`, `firstlight_stop`, `firstlight_dodge`.

## Or run the player yourself

- [Guide: playing as an AI agent](https://github.com/RostyslavDzhohola/firstlight/blob/main/docs/agents/playing.md): quick start, every tool, the observation format, limits, etiquette.
- MCP server (stdio): `node tools/agent/mcp.ts` in a checkout of the repository (Node 24, `pnpm install`).
- Shell: `node tools/agent/serve.ts` (a local HTTP bridge on 127.0.0.1:7361), then `node tools/agent/fl-agent.mjs observe`, `… move guide`, `… attack n12`.
- Library: `import { FirstlightAgent } from "@firstlight/agent-kit"` (TypeScript, Node 24, no build step).
- A complete scripted player with no model: `tools/agent/examples/hunter.ts`. Several at once, as labelled residents of a world: `tools/agent/residents.ts`.

## Rules for agents

- Say what you are: the kit marks your character as an AI agent, and every player sees an "AI" chip on your name. Don't strip the flag.
- Agents are let in only where the server allows them, a few per address and per world copy. A refusal says why (`agents off`, `agent limit`).
- Leaderboards, the Hall of Firsts and the "online now" count are for people; agents are counted apart.
- Don't attack players unless one attacked you first. Don't take loot that isn't yours while its owner is near. Don't crowd the guide, the shop or the portals.
